pr.title: Put checks that detect UB under their own flag below debug_assertions
pr.author: saethlin

analysis.originalLogic: Both passes treated `-Cdebug-assertions` as the source of truth for UB checks. `InstSimplify::simplify_ub_check` unconditionally rewrote `Rvalue::NullaryOp(NullOp::UbChecks, _)` to a boolean constant computed from `self.tcx.sess.opts.debug_assertions`. `CheckAlignment` enabled the pass from `sess.opts.debug_assertions` (after the i686-pc-windows-msvc exclusion). The corrected source of truth is `Session::ub_checks()`, which is `self.opts.unstable_opts.ub_checks.unwrap_or(self.opts.debug_assertions)`.
analysis.incorrectTransformation: Incorrect transformation: fold `NullOp::UbChecks` to the value of `debug_assertions`, and gate `CheckAlignment` solely on `debug_assertions`. Thus, with `-Cdebug-assertions=yes -Zub-checks=no`, InstSimplify would fold UB-check predicates to true and CheckAlignment would remain enabled, retaining UB checks that should be disabled; with `-Cdebug-assertions=no -Zub-checks=yes`, it would fold them to false and skip CheckAlignment, losing checks that should be enabled. The corrected transformation folds to `sess.ub_checks()` and gates CheckAlignment on `sess.ub_checks()`.
analysis.inputDomain: Rust compilation units containing `NullOp::UbChecks` (including unsafe-precondition checks such as `slice::get_unchecked`, `slice::from_raw_parts`, and `cfg!(ub_checks)`), or alignment-sensitive reference construction handled by CheckAlignment, compiled with `-Zub-checks` and `-Cdebug-assertions` set to divergent values. Relevant combinations are debug assertions enabled with UB checks explicitly disabled, and debug assertions disabled with UB checks explicitly enabled. Optimized builds are important because the incorrect constant folding changes emitted IR and runtime behavior.
analysis.summary: UB-check predicates and the CheckAlignment pass must use the `ub_checks` setting, not `debug_assertions` directly. `-Zub-checks` defaults to `-Cdebug-assertions`, but explicitly overrides it. The historical InstSimplify folding to `debug_assertions`, and CheckAlignment gating on `debug_assertions`, are wrong whenever the two flags diverge: one direction retains UB checks that were explicitly disabled, the other removes UB checks that were explicitly enabled. This patch is flag-separation/feature work, not a confirmed bug-fix PR; no compiler was built or executed here.
analysis.trigger: Compile code containing `NullOp::UbChecks` or alignment-checkable references with `-Zub-checks` explicitly different from `-Cdebug-assertions`, so `sess.ub_checks() != sess.opts.debug_assertions`. Examples from the patch: `-Cdebug-assertions=yes -Zub-checks=no` for the codegen check, and `-Cdebug-assertions=no -Zub-checks=yes` for the runtime-fail precondition checks.
preconditions: The compilation must contain a `NullOp::UbChecks` value or code that CheckAlignment would instrument; otherwise the flag choice has no observable effect.
`-Zub-checks` is optional and defaults to `-Cdebug-assertions`; divergence is required to expose the historical transformation error.
Using `cfg(ub_checks)` in user source requires the `cfg_ub_checks` feature gate, as shown by the E0658 feature-gate test.
CheckAlignment has a separate target exclusion: if `sess.target.llvm_target == "i686-pc-windows-msvc"`, the pass returns false before consulting the UB-check setting.

The intrinsic documentation notes that UB-check evaluation may be delayed until monomorphization when the crate has UB checks enabled or carries `#[rustc_preserve_ub_checks]`, so generic/inline and non-inline paths can differ.
pitfalls: Do not equate `ub_checks` with `debug_assertions`: the default is inheritance, but `-Zub-checks` can explicitly override it in either direction.
Do not confuse `ub_checks` with `overflow_checks`; they are separate gating mechanisms.
`cfg!(debug_assertions)` and `cfg!(ub_checks)` answer different questions once the flags diverge; testing only `cfg!(debug_assertions)` will miss the regression.
A run-pass-only test can miss unwanted checks that remain in optimized IR; inspect codegen/IR when the expected behavior is that a UB check is absent.
Do not overgeneralize from tests that use the default flag value: with no `-Zub-checks`, old and new implementations agree because UB checks inherit debug assertions.
CheckAlignment's target-specific early return must remain in place; changing only the flag gate does not remove that exclusion.
analysis.testStrategy: Use paired/focused Rust tests that change only the UB-check transformation or flag gate. For InstSimplify, add a codegen test compiled with `-O -Cdebug-assertions=yes`, with revisions `DEBUG` and `NOCHECKS` where `NOCHECKS` adds `-Zub-checks=no`; define `pub unsafe fn slice_get_unchecked(x: &[i32], i: usize) -> &i32 { x.get_unchecked(i) }` and FileCheck for `icmp ult`, `br i1`, `call core::panicking::panic_nounwind`, `unreachable` in the enabled case, and `tail call void @llvm.assume` plus `getelementptr inbounds` in the disabled case. For CheckAlignment, use the runtime-fail UI tests with `-Copt-level=3 -Cdebug-assertions=no -Zub-checks=yes` and error patterns `unsafe precondition(s) violated: slice::from_raw_parts` for misaligned/null slices and `slice::get_unchecked requires` for out-of-bounds access. Also use `cfg_ub_checks` run-pass tests: `-Zub-checks=no` must make `cfg!(ub_checks)` false and select the `#[cfg(not(ub_checks))]` function, while `-Zub-checks=yes` must make it true and select `#[cfg(ub_checks)]`; a default test should assert `cfg!(ub_checks) == cfg!(debug_assertions)` under both `-Cdebug-assertions=yes` and `-Cdebug-assertions=no`. Finally, test the feature gate without `#![feature(cfg_ub_checks)]` and expect E0658 with the issue #123499 diagnostic.
evidence: By default, `-Zub-checks` flag inherits the value of `-Cdebug-assertions`.
This test ensures that such a runtime check is *not* emitted when debug-assertions are enabled,
